jobs.description:
Director of Engineering

Overview

We are seeking a Director of Engineering to lead the technical strategy and execution of large-scale industrial energy and infrastructure projects from concept through design, construction, commissioning, and operational handover. This role oversees multidisciplinary engineering teams and external partners to deliver safe, reliable, and high-performance industrial systems, including thermal energy, power generation, and facility infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Lead engineering across the full project lifecycle: concept, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, startup, and handover.
Define engineering standards, technical strategy, and design governance for capital projects.
Manage EPC firms, engineering consultants, OEMs, and vendors to ensure technical quality and alignment with project goals.
Oversee integration of complex systems (thermal utilities, steam/hot water, power generation, electrical distribution, controls, rotating equipment).
Provide cross-discipline technical leadership (mechanical, electrical, civil, process, controls).
Lead technical risk management and resolve complex engineering challenges.
Oversee equipment selection, specifications, and technical bid evaluations.
Ensure compliance with relevant codes, standards, and regulations.
Lead commissioning, performance testing, and operational readiness.
Partner with project, operations, and executive teams to deliver capital projects successfully.
Drive system optimization for safety, reliability, performance, and lifecycle cost.
Support engineering staffing, capability development, budgeting, and organizational growth.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems Engineering, or related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in industrial energy systems, utilities, manufacturing, or large infrastructure.
Proven leadership of multidisciplinary engineering teams at a senior level.
Strong track record delivering full lifecycle industrial capital projects.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred

Experience in petrochemical, manufacturing, district energy, data centers, utilities, or heavy industry.
Exposure to CHP/cogeneration, combined cycle, or integrated energy systems.
EPC/EPCM project delivery experience.
PE license or advanced technical degree.

jobs.title: Director of Software Development
jobs.description:
About Karmak

Karmak is a 100% employee-owned software company that has helped keep the commercial transportation industry moving for more than 40 years. Our flagship platform, Karmak Fusion
, powers the parts, service, accounting, and business operations of heavy-duty truck dealerships and transportation companies across North America. Simply put, our customers keep America moving-and we build the technology that helps them do it.

We develop on the Microsoft technology stack, including .NET, SQL Server, and Microsoft Azure
, creating modern, scalable solutions for a mission-critical industry. As employee-owners, we think beyond our individual roles and share responsibility for our company's success. We're looking for leaders who embrace that same ownership mindset and are excited to make a lasting impact.

Position Summary

Remote (US); limited travel (1–2 trips per year)

The Director of Software Development is responsible for the management and daily execution of Karmak's development organization in support of Karmak Fusion. Leading through four development managers spanning application development, QA, and database/reporting teams (a 30+ person engineering organization), this position owns the flow of work between Support, Implementation, Product, DBA, and the development teams; serves as the development-side approval authority on customer patches; and makes go/no-go decisions across a multi-version release train.

The Director is the primary point of escalation into development for the rest of the organization and the VP of Development's operational right hand - a role requiring the technical credibility to challenge a root-cause analysis, the judgment to weigh customer risk on every patch and release decision, and the leadership to run cross-team incident response when a customer-impacting issue crosses team boundaries.

How You'll Operate

This role is built for a high-agency leader. Here is the working relationship you should expect:

You'll get context and priorities from the VP of Development - not task lists. We expect you to identify what will move the needle, commit to outcomes, and run with them. You bring the VP problems with proposed answers, not open questions.
This is not a hands-on coding role, but you haven't stopped being an engineer. You can read C# and SQL, sit in architecture and root-cause reviews and challenge them, and tell a real fix from a symptom patch. Senior engineers respect you because of it.
You own escalations end to end: you move them, you don't track them. When plans change, you re-plan in hours, not weeks, and keep the train moving.
You communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided. Exceptions come with verified data, options, and a recommendation.

What You'll Own In Year One

Success in this role is measured in outcomes, not activity. In your first year, a home run looks like:

Release predictability - Releases and patches across the multi-version release train ship on schedule with fewer defect escapes, and go/no-go discipline holds at every checkpoint - without the VP in the room.
Escalations owned and closed - Escalations from Support, Implementation, and Product get a single accountable owner, are driven to root cause rather than symptom fixes, and are closed with clear communication - they stop bouncing upward.
AI-assisted development adoption - The organization measurably advances on AI-assisted engineering - code analysis, automated review, test automation, and agentic tooling - with honest evaluation of where it multiplies velocity and where it doesn't.
Manager bench strength - The four development managers grow into leaders who plan, prioritize, and make sound calls with less direction - the organization runs well when you step away from it.

Essential Job Functions

Provide technical leadership and direction to the development managers and their teams, assisting with planning, prioritization, technology assessment, professional development, and cross-team coordination
Serve as the development-side approval authority on customer patches, weighing patch-versus-upgrade paths, deployment risk windows, and multi-version complexity; ensure patch decisions protect both the customer and the maintainability of the release line
Own go/no-go decisions at each release checkpoint - integration close, QA greenlight, smoke test, packaging, and staged customer rollout - including the authority to hold or pause a release when quality or customer risk demands it
Serve as the primary point of escalation to development for Support, Implementation, and Product; route issues to the correct team or subject-matter expert, chase them to closure, and keep requestors informed with clear status and next steps
Lead incident response for customer-impacting issues that cross team boundaries; drive to root cause rather than symptom fixes, convene the right people quickly, and communicate resolution paths to stakeholders
Direct the daily product delivery rhythm in partnership with Support, DBA, Installations, and Product, and chair recurring quality reviews with the support organization, converting findings into tracked work items
Keep the VP of Development ahead of surprises: escalate exceptions with verified data, options, and a recommendation; draft customer-facing technical communications for executive review
Manage relationships with external technical consultants and vendors in support of development initiatives
Champion continuous improvement of engineering practice, including branch and merge policy, automated code review, test automation, and AI-assisted development tooling
Manage the personnel activities of the team to include hiring, training, and evaluating employees; lead merit and salary planning through the development managers
Lead the team in change management and effectively apply new process improvements
Embrace self-development, professional growth, and desire for feedback for individual growth
Maintain confidentiality
Be a champion for Karmak and the team

Essential Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.S.) in Computer Science or a related field and a minimum of 10 years of software development experience, including 5+ years leading developers and experience managing managers or an organization of 30+ engineers; or equivalent combination of education and experience
Required: current technical depth on the Microsoft development stack - able to read and reason about .NET code (C#/VB.NET) and Microsoft SQL Server (T-SQL, database design, query performance) well enough to be credible with senior engineers, interrogate a root-cause analysis, and distinguish a real fix from a symptom patch
Strongly preferred: experience running teams that build and operate on Microsoft Azure (PaaS services, cloud architecture) and Azure DevOps for work tracking, pipelines, and release management
Direct experience owning production release and patch decisions for commercial, customer-installed or hosted software, including versioned release trains and customer-impact risk assessment; ERP or other business-critical domain experience strongly preferred
A demonstrated pattern of high-agency ownership: identifying what matters, driving it to done without waiting for direction, and being accountable for outcomes, not just process
Demonstrated pattern of calm incident leadership and cross-functional coordination across support, QA, DBA, and product organizations
Exceptional team leadership skills, including the ability to effectively coach, motivate, and empower team members and develop the judgment of front-line managers
Ability to build and sustain trusted relationships internally and externally, sound judgment in dealing with business issues, and the instinct to communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided
Strong initiative, teamwork, and interpersonal skills; strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting customer-facing technical communications
Capable of working in a growth-oriented environment, with ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent requests, projects, and responsibilities
Hands-on experience adopting AI-assisted development practices (code analysis, automated review, agentic tooling) preferred
Knowledge of the heavy-duty or commercial transportation industry a plus

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. Additional responsibilities may be assigned by Karmak.

What You Will Have An Opportunity To Do

Director of Engineering

Department:
Engineering / Maintenance

Reports To:
General Manager

Location:
Chaminade Resort & Spa

Employment Type:
Full-Time

Exempt Status:
Exempt

Salary Range:
$100,000–$120,000 annually, negotiable based on experience and qualifications

Position Summary

The Director of Engineering is a hands-on working leader
responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance, repair, and overall condition of Chaminade Resort & Spa’s physical property. This position requires a strong technical background and an individual who is comfortable working alongside the Engineering team—not simply directing from an office.

The Director of Engineering will lead by example, personally assisting with troubleshooting, repairs, preventative maintenance, inspections, projects, and emergency response. This position is responsible for ensuring that guest rooms, public spaces, back-of-house areas, mechanical systems, grounds, recreational facilities, and resort infrastructure are maintained to the highest standards of safety, functionality, and appearance.

The ideal candidate is a working engineer and strong leader
who can diagnose problems, pick up a tool when needed, teach the team, prioritize work, and hold themselves and others accountable for maintaining a premier resort property.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Hands-On Engineering & Maintenance

Serve as an active, working member of the Engineering team and regularly perform maintenance and repair work throughout the property.
Personally troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical, HVAC, mechanical, carpentry, appliance, and general building maintenance issues.
Respond directly to guest room and public area maintenance calls when needed.
Perform preventative maintenance inspections and repairs throughout the resort.
Conduct daily property walks to identify maintenance, safety, cleanliness, and appearance concerns.
Inspect guest rooms, meeting spaces, public areas, back-of-house areas, pools, spa facilities, recreational areas, and grounds.
Assist Engineering team members with complex repairs and technical issues.
Train team members through hands-on demonstration and coaching.
Maintain tools, equipment, mechanical rooms, workshops, and Engineering storage areas in a clean, organized, and professional condition.
Be willing and able to work alongside the team during periods of high workload, staffing shortages, emergencies, or major projects.
Respond to emergency maintenance situations and facility-related guest concerns quickly and professionally.

Building Systems & Equipment

Maintain and troubleshoot HVAC systems, electrical systems, plumbing, pumps, water systems, boilers, appliances, lighting, mechanical equipment, and other property systems.
Oversee and personally participate in preventative maintenance programs.
Monitor building automation and energy management systems.
Maintain pools, spas, water features, and related mechanical and chemical systems in accordance with applicable requirements.
Ensure fire/life safety systems and emergency equipment are properly maintained and inspected.
Maintain accurate records of equipment, repairs, inspections, warranties, and preventative maintenance.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead the Engineering team through a hands-on management approach.
Set the standard for work quality, urgency, professionalism, and guest service.
Work alongside Engineering associates and provide coaching and technical guidance in real time.
Train team members on proper repair techniques, preventative maintenance, safety procedures, and equipment operation.
Schedule and assign daily work based on occupancy, guest needs, property priorities, and staffing levels.
Monitor completion and quality of work orders.
Hold team members accountable for performance, attendance, productivity, safety, and department standards.
Create a culture where the Engineering team takes pride in the appearance and condition of the resort.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, performance management, and development of Engineering associates.

Preventative Maintenance

Develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive preventative maintenance program.
Establish recurring inspection and maintenance schedules for guest rooms, equipment, mechanical systems, and facilities.
Track completion of preventative maintenance and identify recurring issues.
Analyze equipment failures and determine root causes to reduce repeat repairs.
Proactively identify aging equipment and recommend replacement or improvement.
Ensure guest rooms and facilities are returned to excellent condition following repairs.

Capital Projects & Renovations

Assist with planning, coordinating, and executing capital improvement projects.
Be actively involved in renovation and construction projects from planning through completion.
Perform hands-on work when appropriate and coordinate Engineering labor to support projects.
Manage contractors and vendors while ensuring work meets property standards.
Inspect completed work and identify deficiencies requiring correction.
Minimize disruption to guests and hotel operations during projects.
Maintain documentation related to projects, equipment, warranties, and completed work.

Budget & Financial Management

Develop and manage the Engineering department operating budget.
Monitor labor, supplies, repair costs, utilities, equipment, and outside service expenses.
Identify opportunities to reduce expenses through preventative maintenance and efficient operations.
Evaluate whether repairs should be completed internally or contracted to outside vendors.
Maintain appropriate inventory of parts, tools, supplies, and equipment.
Obtain quotes and manage vendor relationships.
Review invoices and service agreements for accuracy and value.

Safety & Compliance

Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, building codes, and safety requirements.
Maintain required permits, inspections, licenses, and certifications.
Oversee fire/life safety inspections, testing, and maintenance.
Ensure proper pool and spa maintenance and water quality.
Maintain OSHA and workplace safety standards.
Ensure proper storage, handling, and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials.
Conduct regular safety inspections and immediately address hazards.
Participate in emergency preparedness and response procedures.

Energy & Sustainability

Monitor utility usage and identify opportunities to reduce energy and water consumption.
Maintain HVAC, lighting, plumbing, and other systems for maximum efficiency.
Identify equipment or operational changes that can reduce utility costs.
Support resort sustainability and environmental initiatives.

Guest Service

Recognize that Engineering is a critical part of the overall guest experience.
Respond promptly and professionally to guest maintenance concerns.
Follow up on recurring guest room issues and ensure problems are permanently resolved.
Partner with Front Office, Housekeeping, Food & Beverage, Spa, Recreation, and other departments to resolve property-related issues.
Maintain a professional and service-oriented presence throughout the resort.
Take ownership of property issues rather than simply passing them along to others.

Qualifications

Minimum 5 years of progressive engineering, maintenance, or facilities experience, preferably within a full-service hotel or resort.
Previous Engineering leadership or supervisory experience required.
Strong hands-on technical knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, mechanical systems, carpentry, and general building maintenance.
Demonstrated ability to personally troubleshoot and complete repairs.
Experience leading and developing a maintenance or engineering team.
Experience with preventative maintenance programs.
Strong understanding of hotel operations and the importance of guest service.
Experience with budgets, purchasing, vendors, contractors, and capital projects.
Knowledge of applicable building, safety, environmental, and fire/life safety regulations.
Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.
Excellent communication and organizational skills.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects and emergency situations.
Computer proficiency and experience with computerized maintenance management systems preferred.
Engineering, facilities, construction, or trade certifications are preferred.
Must be comfortable working with tools and performing hands-on maintenance and repair work on a regular basis.

Physical Requirements

This is a hands-on operational position
requiring regular physical activity.

Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, crawl, climb ladders and stairs, and work in confined or elevated spaces.
Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull equipment, tools, and materials.
Ability to safely operate hand tools and power tools.
Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Ability to respond quickly to emergency situations throughout the resort.
Ability to perform physical maintenance and repair tasks as required.

Hands-On Leadership
Technical Troubleshooting
Mechanical Aptitude
Preventative Maintenance
Team Development
Guest Service

With over four decades of expertise, we partner with some of the world’s most influential companies to design and optimize environments that demand precision, scalability, and resilience.

Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.

The Power Engineering Director will serve as the senior technical and operational leader for the practice, partnering with executive leadership to set strategy, develop engineering standards, drive business development, and build the team and capabilities necessary to scale.

The Power Engineering Director operates with a high degree of autonomy, receiving strategic direction from executive leadership. This role is responsible for leading engineering teams, driving strategic initiatives, supporting organizational planning, and developing the people, processes, and technical capabilities necessary to scale the practice. As the practice matures, the Director may also be called upon to support executive leadership in evaluating strategic M&A or partnership opportunities that could accelerate Power Solutions growth, expand delivery capabilities, or add technical depth to the team.

Monitor and communicate engineering quality, delivery performance, and client satisfaction metrics across the practice portfolio; escalate risks and issues to executive leadership with recommended corrective actions.

Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll lead high-impact incident response work in a complex cloud environment and help shape how Atlassian responds to security events at scale. You’ll lead or coordinate complex security incidents, bringing structure, urgency, and sound judgment under pressure. You’ll partner with Detection, Security Engineering, Product Security, Legal, Crisis Communications, Support, and senior leadership to drive investigation, containment, recovery, and follow-through. You’ll directly manage a team of 5-8 in the US region.

You’ll coach incident responders and senior practitioners, raising the quality of investigations, handoffs, decision-making, and executive communication. You’ll improve the incident response system through playbooks, metrics, exercises, post-incident reviews, and better tooling. A key part of the role will be driving the adoption of investigative AI tools and automation that help analysts triage faster, surface relevant signals, reduce toil, and improve consistency without compromising judgment or security rigor.

You’ll also support regulated and high-trust environments, including work that requires a strong understanding of formal incident handling, reporting expectations, and documented operating procedures.

What You’ll Bring

On day one, we’ll expect you to bring a strong mix of incident leadership, operational maturity, and people leadership. You’ll have experience directly leading complex, multi-stakeholder security incidents in a SaaS, cloud, or enterprise environment, along with demonstrated success managing and developing senior security engineers, incident responders, and/or technical leads.

You’ll have strong executive communication skills, including the ability to translate incomplete technical information into clear decisions, risks, and next steps. You’ll have experience improving incident response programs through metrics, retrospectives, process design, readiness exercises, and cross-team influence, as well as hands-on familiarity with investigation workflows, detection and response tooling, log analysis, and operational coordination across globally distributed teams.

You should have experience deploying investigative AI tools and automation in security operations or incident response environments, including using automation to reduce analyst toil, improve triage quality, accelerate investigations, enrich cases, retrieve relevant knowledge, summarize findings, or orchestrate response workflows. You’ll also bring strong systems thinking: the ability to connect incidents to broader improvements in telemetry, detection logic, escalation paths, tooling, and operating models, together with calm, structured decision-making in ambiguous, high-pressure situations.

What Will Set You Apart

Experience serving as an incident commander or major incident manager for high-severity cyber incidents will help you stand out, as will experience supporting regulated environments or formal incident reporting obligations, including government or FedRAMP-adjacent contexts. We’ll value experience building or scaling follow-the-sun incident response models across regions and introducing AI-assisted investigation workflows, case enrichment, knowledge retrieval, summarization, or orchestration capabilities in security operations.

Strong understanding of how to use operational metrics, quality signals, and error patterns to guide program investments is valuable, as is experience speaking externally, representing security programs, or contributing to broader security community practices.

Our team culture

The Incident Response team values calm execution, clear communication, and continuous learning. We are collaborative, direct, and low-ego during incidents, and we expect leaders to care about both outcomes and the health of the people doing the work. We use blameless review, measurable improvement, and thoughtful automation to get better over time. We want leaders who can set a high bar while creating trust, psychological safety, and accountability across regions and functions.

Why this role matters

This is a rare opportunity to lead one of the most important security functions in a global software company. You’ll influence how Atlassian handles major incidents, matures its response capabilities, and invests in the future of security operations. You’ll work on meaningful problems at the intersection of incident command, operations, engineering, and trust, help define how investigative AI and automation can responsibly improve security response at scale, and partner with senior security and business leaders while building durable systems, stronger responders, and better outcomes for customers.

About Karmak

Karmak is a 100% employee-owned software company that has helped keep the commercial transportation industry moving for more than 40 years. Our flagship platform, Karmak Fusion
, powers the parts, service, accounting, and business operations of heavy-duty truck dealerships and transportation companies across North America. Simply put, our customers keep America moving-and we build the technology that helps them do it.

We develop on the Microsoft technology stack, including .NET, SQL Server, and Microsoft Azure
, creating modern, scalable solutions for a mission-critical industry. As employee-owners, we think beyond our individual roles and share responsibility for our company's success. We're looking for leaders who embrace that same ownership mindset and are excited to make a lasting impact.

Position Summary

Remote (US); limited travel (1–2 trips per year)

The Director of Software Development is responsible for the management and daily execution of Karmak's development organization in support of Karmak Fusion. Leading through four development managers spanning application development, QA, and database/reporting teams (a 30+ person engineering organization), this position owns the flow of work between Support, Implementation, Product, DBA, and the development teams; serves as the development-side approval authority on customer patches; and makes go/no-go decisions across a multi-version release train.

The Director is the primary point of escalation into development for the rest of the organization and the VP of Development's operational right hand - a role requiring the technical credibility to challenge a root-cause analysis, the judgment to weigh customer risk on every patch and release decision, and the leadership to run cross-team incident response when a customer-impacting issue crosses team boundaries.

How You'll Operate

This role is built for a high-agency leader. Here is the working relationship you should expect:

You'll get context and priorities from the VP of Development - not task lists. We expect you to identify what will move the needle, commit to outcomes, and run with them. You bring the VP problems with proposed answers, not open questions.
This is not a hands-on coding role, but you haven't stopped being an engineer. You can read C# and SQL, sit in architecture and root-cause reviews and challenge them, and tell a real fix from a symptom patch. Senior engineers respect you because of it.
You own escalations end to end: you move them, you don't track them. When plans change, you re-plan in hours, not weeks, and keep the train moving.
You communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided. Exceptions come with verified data, options, and a recommendation.

What You'll Own In Year One

Success in this role is measured in outcomes, not activity. In your first year, a home run looks like:

Release predictability - Releases and patches across the multi-version release train ship on schedule with fewer defect escapes, and go/no-go discipline holds at every checkpoint - without the VP in the room.
Escalations owned and closed - Escalations from Support, Implementation, and Product get a single accountable owner, are driven to root cause rather than symptom fixes, and are closed with clear communication - they stop bouncing upward.
AI-assisted development adoption - The organization measurably advances on AI-assisted engineering - code analysis, automated review, test automation, and agentic tooling - with honest evaluation of where it multiplies velocity and where it doesn't.
Manager bench strength - The four development managers grow into leaders who plan, prioritize, and make sound calls with less direction - the organization runs well when you step away from it.

Essential Job Functions

Provide technical leadership and direction to the development managers and their teams, assisting with planning, prioritization, technology assessment, professional development, and cross-team coordination
Serve as the development-side approval authority on customer patches, weighing patch-versus-upgrade paths, deployment risk windows, and multi-version complexity; ensure patch decisions protect both the customer and the maintainability of the release line
Own go/no-go decisions at each release checkpoint - integration close, QA greenlight, smoke test, packaging, and staged customer rollout - including the authority to hold or pause a release when quality or customer risk demands it
Serve as the primary point of escalation to development for Support, Implementation, and Product; route issues to the correct team or subject-matter expert, chase them to closure, and keep requestors informed with clear status and next steps
Lead incident response for customer-impacting issues that cross team boundaries; drive to root cause rather than symptom fixes, convene the right people quickly, and communicate resolution paths to stakeholders
Direct the daily product delivery rhythm in partnership with Support, DBA, Installations, and Product, and chair recurring quality reviews with the support organization, converting findings into tracked work items
Keep the VP of Development ahead of surprises: escalate exceptions with verified data, options, and a recommendation; draft customer-facing technical communications for executive review
Manage relationships with external technical consultants and vendors in support of development initiatives
Champion continuous improvement of engineering practice, including branch and merge policy, automated code review, test automation, and AI-assisted development tooling
Manage the personnel activities of the team to include hiring, training, and evaluating employees; lead merit and salary planning through the development managers
Lead the team in change management and effectively apply new process improvements
Embrace self-development, professional growth, and desire for feedback for individual growth
Maintain confidentiality
Be a champion for Karmak and the team

Essential Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.S.) in Computer Science or a related field and a minimum of 10 years of software development experience, including 5+ years leading developers and experience managing managers or an organization of 30+ engineers; or equivalent combination of education and experience
Required: current technical depth on the Microsoft development stack - able to read and reason about .NET code (C#/VB.NET) and Microsoft SQL Server (T-SQL, database design, query performance) well enough to be credible with senior engineers, interrogate a root-cause analysis, and distinguish a real fix from a symptom patch
Strongly preferred: experience running teams that build and operate on Microsoft Azure (PaaS services, cloud architecture) and Azure DevOps for work tracking, pipelines, and release management
Direct experience owning production release and patch decisions for commercial, customer-installed or hosted software, including versioned release trains and customer-impact risk assessment; ERP or other business-critical domain experience strongly preferred
A demonstrated pattern of high-agency ownership: identifying what matters, driving it to done without waiting for direction, and being accountable for outcomes, not just process
Demonstrated pattern of calm incident leadership and cross-functional coordination across support, QA, DBA, and product organizations
Exceptional team leadership skills, including the ability to effectively coach, motivate, and empower team members and develop the judgment of front-line managers
Ability to build and sustain trusted relationships internally and externally, sound judgment in dealing with business issues, and the instinct to communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided
Strong initiative, teamwork, and interpersonal skills; strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting customer-facing technical communications
Capable of working in a growth-oriented environment, with ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent requests, projects, and responsibilities
Hands-on experience adopting AI-assisted development practices (code analysis, automated review, agentic tooling) preferred
Knowledge of the heavy-duty or commercial transportation industry a plus

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. Additional responsibilities may be assigned by Karmak.

Exempt

Serve as an active, working member of the Engineering team and regularly perform maintenance and repair work throughout the property.
Personally troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical, HVAC, mechanical, carpentry, appliance, and general building maintenance issues.
Respond directly to guest room and public area maintenance calls when needed.
Perform preventative maintenance inspections and repairs throughout the resort.
Conduct daily property walks to identify maintenance, safety, cleanliness, and appearance concerns.
Inspect guest rooms, meeting spaces, public areas, back-of-house areas, pools, spa facilities, recreational areas, and grounds.
Assist Engineering team members with complex repairs and technical issues.
Train team members through hands-on demonstration and coaching.
Maintain tools, equipment, mechanical rooms, workshops, and Engineering storage areas in a clean, organized, and professional condition.

Monitor building automation and energy management systems.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll lead high-impact incident response work in a complex cloud environment and help shape how Atlassian responds to security events at scale. You’ll lead or coordinate complex security incidents, bringing structure, urgency, and sound judgment under pressure. You’ll partner with Detection, Security Engineering, Product Security, Legal, Crisis Communications, Support, and senior leadership to drive investigation, containment, recovery, and follow-through. You’ll directly manage a team of 5-8 in the US region.

You’ll coach incident responders and senior practitioners, raising the quality of investigations, handoffs, decision-making, and executive communication. You’ll improve the incident response system through playbooks, metrics, exercises, post-incident reviews, and better tooling. A key part of the role will be driving the adoption of investigative AI tools and automation that help analysts triage faster, surface relevant signals, reduce toil, and improve consistency without compromising judgment or security rigor.

You’ll also support regulated and high-trust environments, including work that requires a strong understanding of formal incident handling, reporting expectations, and documented operating procedures.

What You’ll Bring

On day one, we’ll expect you to bring a strong mix of incident leadership, operational maturity, and people leadership. You’ll have experience directly leading complex, multi-stakeholder security incidents in a SaaS, cloud, or enterprise environment, along with demonstrated success managing and developing senior security engineers, incident responders, and/or technical leads.

You’ll have strong executive communication skills, including the ability to translate incomplete technical information into clear decisions, risks, and next steps. You’ll have experience improving incident response programs through metrics, retrospectives, process design, readiness exercises, and cross-team influence, as well as hands-on familiarity with investigation workflows, detection and response tooling, log analysis, and operational coordination across globally distributed teams.

You should have experience deploying investigative AI tools and automation in security operations or incident response environments, including using automation to reduce analyst toil, improve triage quality, accelerate investigations, enrich cases, retrieve relevant knowledge, summarize findings, or orchestrate response workflows. You’ll also bring strong systems thinking: the ability to connect incidents to broader improvements in telemetry, detection logic, escalation paths, tooling, and operating models, together with calm, structured decision-making in ambiguous, high-pressure situations.

What Will Set You Apart

Experience serving as an incident commander or major incident manager for high-severity cyber incidents will help you stand out, as will experience supporting regulated environments or formal incident reporting obligations, including government or FedRAMP-adjacent contexts. We’ll value experience building or scaling follow-the-sun incident response models across regions and introducing AI-assisted investigation workflows, case enrichment, knowledge retrieval, summarization, or orchestration capabilities in security operations.

Strong understanding of how to use operational metrics, quality signals, and error patterns to guide program investments is valuable, as is experience speaking externally, representing security programs, or contributing to broader security community practices.

Our team culture

The Incident Response team values calm execution, clear communication, and continuous learning. We are collaborative, direct, and low-ego during incidents, and we expect leaders to care about both outcomes and the health of the people doing the work. We use blameless review, measurable improvement, and thoughtful automation to get better over time. We want leaders who can set a high bar while creating trust, psychological safety, and accountability across regions and functions.

Why this role matters

This is a rare opportunity to lead one of the most important security functions in a global software company. You’ll influence how Atlassian handles major incidents, matures its response capabilities, and invests in the future of security operations. You’ll work on meaningful problems at the intersection of incident command, operations, engineering, and trust, help define how investigative AI and automation can responsibly improve security response at scale, and partner with senior security and business leaders while building durable systems, stronger responders, and better outcomes for customers.

new_jobs.title: Vice President of Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Sigma360 (www.sigma360.com) is redefining how financial institutions detect and prevent financial crime. We are venture backed, founder-led and build advanced risk intelligence and screening technology that helps compliance teams move faster, make better decisions, and stop bad actors at scale.

Our platform sits at the intersection of big data, AI, and mission-critical financial infrastructure.
We are entering a key growth phase and are looking for an exceptional engineering leader to help scale our platform, engineering and data team, and technical vision.

We’re a super collaborative team that values ownership, clarity, and practical problem solving.

The Role
We are hiring a hands-on engineering leader who has helped scale technology companies from Series A/B through high-growth stages. This is a builder’s role: you’ll set technical direction, grow and lead a high-performing team, and stay close to the architecture and code powering our data and intelligence platform. You will work directly with the CEO to define and execute on the technical aspects of the business.

You’ll also partner closely with Product, Data, and Go-To-Market leadership to deliver a platform that is scalable, resilient, and built for the future of AI-driven financial crime detection.

IMPORTANT: We are looking for candidates who have scaled ventures versus worked a scaled firms. If you scaled within a big firm, make that explicit and please explain your desire to join a smaller breakout firm like ours.

What You’ll Do

Technical Leadership
Own the architecture and evolution of Sigma360’s core platform, with a strong focus on big data, distributed systems, and AI-ready infrastructure
Make high-quality, pragmatic technical decisions that balance speed, scalability, and long-term maintainability
Stay hands-on in system design, code reviews, and key technical initiatives

Team Building & Scaling
Recruit, develop, and lead a world-class engineering team across backend, data, and platform engineering
Build strong engineering culture, processes, and delivery discipline while preserving startup velocity
Mentor senior engineers and emerging leaders; create clear growth paths

Platform & Data Excellence
Oversee the design of large-scale data ingestion, enrichment, and search systems
Ensure our platform can handle massive, complex, and evolving datasets used in financial crime and risk intelligence without fail
Drive best practices in performance, reliability, observability, and security
Measure, report on, and optimize infrastructure spend

Execution & Cross-Functional Partnership
Work closely with Product and Data teams to translate complex risk and compliance needs into scalable technical solutions
Partner with leadership to align engineering roadmaps with company strategy and growth milestones
Help the company scale from startup execution to durable, repeatable delivery

What We’re Looking For

Experience
10+ years in software engineering, with significant time in high-growth startup environments or the equivalent someplace else (important)
Proven experience scaling engineering teams and systems from Series A/B through rapid growth and interfacing with executive leadership, the board and high-level clients
Experience building and operating data-intensive, distributed systems at scale

Technical Depth
Strong background in big data architectures (e.g., streaming, ETL/ELT pipelines, large-scale search, graph or entity resolution systems)
Experience with modern data and cloud stacks (e.g., AWS/GCP/Azure, Kubernetes, data warehouses/lakes, real-time processing)
Exposure to AI/ML applications, including leveraging of LLMs for intelligent data triage, matching and workflow automation, including familiarity with latest approaches
Comfortable going deep in system design and code when needed — this is not a purely managerial role

Leadership & Mindset
A player-coach who leads by example and earns trust through technical credibility
High ownership mentality with the ability to operate in ambiguity
Strong problem solving skills to help unblock the team
Passion for using the latest technologies in practical, production-grade ways
Strong communicator who can align engineers, product leaders, and executives

Nice to Haves
Experience in financial services, fintech, or financial crime/AML/compliance technology
Exposure to AI/ML-driven products and data science platform needs
Experience with highly regulated or mission-critical software environments
New York (and/or surrounding region) strongly preferred

Why This Role Matters
Your work will directly power systems that help stop fraud, corruption, trafficking, and financial crime globally. You’ll shape not just our engineering org, but the technical foundation of a company set on becoming the category leader in risk and compliance intelligence.

If you’re excited to build serious technology, with real-world impact, at startup speed — we’d love to talk.
